newsitem.title: USA: Fund liquidation presses CME cattle to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Fund liquidation presses CME cattle to lower close.

text.p: CME live as well as feeder cattle futures fell sharply to day's lows late as fundamental pressure pushed futures down into fund liquidation sell stops, traders said.

Talk of lower cash cattle trade and a recent weakening in boxed beef prices added to early pressure from Friday's bearish USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report to knock live cattle futures prices into fund sell stops.
Feeder cattle futures followed, with higher corn futures also weighing on values in that pit, traders said.
Short covering developed in live cattle futures after initial losses linked to the report, but fell when cash cattle traded lower.

Live cattle futures closed 1.150 to 0.025 cent a lb lower with December off most at 65.825 cents. Distant August posted a new contract low of 62.000 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.900 cent lower to unchanged with January off most at 64.825 cents.

"Without an active fed steer trade, futures were about to try to come back and close OK. But when that lower cash market surfaced then everybody backed out" of futures, said Dennis Smith, broker with LIT division of First Options.
Smith noted the $2 per cwt decline in fed steer trade which developed late Monday morning. The drop sparked selling in live cattle with fund liquidation adding to losses, he added.

Traders cited early pressure from Friday's monthly USDA cattle report, which showed the number of cattle in feedyards as of November 1 in the seven key states up one percent from a year ago while placements on feed during October were up 11 percent from a year ago, both above pre-report estimates. October marketings which were down seven percent from last year and under the low end of projections, added to weakness in December, they said.

Sell stops were hit below 66.300 cents a lb in December and closing sell stops kept that month at the day's low. There was early selling in December 66 puts but traders turned buyers on the break. There were also rest conversions in June, buying of 64 calls and selling 60 puts, pit sources said.
RBH and R.J. O'Brien were net sellers while Refco, ING and FIMAT Futures USA sold late, Pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle and fell late on fund liquidation. Cargill Investor Services, LIT division/First Options and ING were notable sellers late, traders said.
Higher corn futures, weaker cash cattle prices after USDA's data and a lower CME feeder cattle index also weighed on prices, they added. The index fell $0.19 to $64.26 per cwt.
